title: Introduce retry dialects, credential mesh, and stream flush ergonomics across Py/TS/Go SDKs
author: Ayesha Khan
description: Motivation: Align retry semantics and credential orchestration across the three official SDKs to reduce customer-facing inconsistencies and to provide explicit, operator-friendly retry profiles. This PR introduces a small, explicit RetryDialect schema (aggressive | safe | hedged) that can be expressed in SDK clients and routed to the runtime where applicable, a lightweight "credential mesh" orchestrator that deterministically funnels multiple credential sources with fallbacks and telemetry, and a stream.flush() primitive to improve generator/pullstream graceful shutdown and immediate buffer draining. Changes are coordinated across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs and include implementation, tests, docs, and version bumps. Checklist: - implement RetryDialect schema (Py/TS/Go) - implement credential mesh and fallback chain - add stream.flush/flushNow primitive for async generators/pullstreams - wire telemetry hooks for retries and credential decisions - update migration guide and changelog - bump SDK versions for release Compatibility: default RetryDialect="safe" keeps existing client behavior; credential mesh is opt-in via Configuration. stream.flush is additive and does not change existing stream semantics unless invoked. Related work: ENG-2468, ENG-2470. Notes for release engineers: coordinate simultaneous SDK tags and publish sequence: python -> typescript -> go to reduce transient compatibility issues for multi-language clients.

notes: This PR coordinates cross-language ergonomics: keep changes small per-language but consistent conceptually. Telemetry hooks added will help us iterate on hedged retry defaults after rollout. The credential mesh intentionally keeps decision logic local to the client so server-side compatibility remains unchanged.
